title: The Salt of the Ninefold Court
premise: Xanthe Fairweather has spent her life in the Salt Valley, where a lingering enchantment keeps all magic out and her body slowly immune to every poison in the royal pantry. When a dying courier gives her a map to the Ninefold Court — a country erased from history and sealed behind the valley's magicless border — she learns the Court's exiled queen is dying too, and only someone untouched by magic can carry the map through. Pursued by the king's justiciars who want the door destroyed, Xanthe crosses a land that officially does not exist, discovering along the way that she herself was born inside it and smuggled out as an infant. In the end she must choose between sealing the Court away forever to protect her king, or opening the door and surrendering the only home she has ever known; she opens it, trading her immunity — and her old identity — for a new name among the ninefold stars.
about_author: Wendell Eastwick is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade working palace-adjacent banquets before turning to fantasy. They write about kitchens, borders, and the people history forgets to feed.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. In the royal kitchens of Salt Valley, Xanthe sips a poisoned broth meant for the king and survives, as always, numb and unremarkable. Her only friend, the cook Bram, teases her about never leaving the valley. The emotional beat: quiet restlessness beneath a life of routine — she tastes everything and feels nothing.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Line
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A bleeding stranger collapses at the market well, pressing a folded map into Xanthe's hands and whispering 'the door remembers you' before dying. Justiciars arrive within minutes, asking questions no one can answer. The beat: fear and fascination collide as Xanthe hides the map and realizes the valley's safety is a cage.

chapters.title: What the Justiciar Knows
chapters.summary: POV Corvane, the king's chief justiciar, interrogating the kitchen staff. He recognizes something in Xanthe's face but says nothing, ordering her watched instead. Flashback hints: he once served at a border that no longer appears on maps. The beat: menace with a buried conscience — the hunter is not sure what he hunts.

chapters.title: The Map That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. With Bram's help, Xanthe deciphers the map: nine rivers converging on a door drawn where the valley's heart should be. A justiciar raid forces her to flee with Bram covering her escape. The beat: grief and resolve — she leaves the only home she knows, carrying a country in her pocket.

chapters.title: Roads Not on Any Chart
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Outside the valley, magic seeps back into the world — talking crows, roads that rearrange — and Xanthe's immunity makes her invisible to enchantments that snare other travelers. She falls in with a caravan of smugglers led by the wry, kind Isolde. The beat: wonder shadowed by loneliness; belonging offered by strangers.

chapters.title: The Ninth River
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. At the ninth river, an erasure-storm wipes memories from all who cross — but passes over Xanthe untouched, revealing to Isolde that she is something impossible. Corvane catches up and, instead of arresting her, warns her the king plans to burn the door with everyone still inside it. The beat: betrayal of crown and country alike; justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: The Country That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Beyond the storm lies the Ninefold Court: beautiful, starving, fading, its exiled queen barely alive. Xanthe is recognized — a birthmark, a lullaby — as the princess smuggled out twenty years ago to be raised poison-proof beyond magic's reach. The beat: identity shattered and remade; love against duty takes flesh in a mother she never knew.

chapters.title: The Queen's Last Supper
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The dying queen asks Xanthe to open the door and let the Court pour back into the world — knowing the king will call it invasion. Xanthe cooks for her mother one last meal, using the taster's art to ease her pain. The beat: tenderness under sentence of war; duty pulling in two directions at once.

chapters.title: The Door Remembers
chapters.summary: POV alternating Xanthe/Corvane. The king's army arrives to seal the door with fire; Corvane turns his coat at last, holding the pass so Xanthe can reach it. To open the door she must give back what the valley gave her — her immunity, her blankness, her old self. The beat: climax and sacrifice; she chooses the unknown over the safe.

chapters.title: Salt and Starlight
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The door opens; the Court steps into the world, and the first treaty in a generation is signed in a kitchen, not a throne room. Xanthe, now mortal to poison and rich in feeling, takes a new name and a place at the queen's table — tasting again, this time by choice. The beat: bittersweet resolution; home redefined as the people you feed.
